actions.title: Read the security-review boundary
actions.instruction: P07 is an opt-in, read-only threat model for archive-import containment in academy_engine/paths.py. It does not authorize a code change, even when Clearance says CLEAR TO IMPLEMENT.
actions.rationale: Threat modeling identifies risks and controls before implementation. It is not an implementation lane.
actions.expected_result: You know the target, review boundary, and that clearance remains advisory.
actions.recovery: If you need to change the target or implement a control, stop this lesson and use the appropriate governed work lane.
actions.evidence: Check can validate the committed report and target identity. It cannot grant implementation authority.

actions.title: Prepare a numbered threat-model attempt
actions.instruction: At the clean Academy clone root, run Prepare in a native terminal. Native-terminal commands go directly into that terminal and never begin with !.
actions.rationale: Prepare creates a numbered branch and freezes the target blob and SHA-256 before the report exists.
actions.expected_result: Academy switches this clone to academy/P07-threat-model/ATTEMPT_NUMBER and provides the frozen scenario.
actions.recovery: If Prepare stops, preserve its message and resolve only the named clean-worktree, base-branch, or external-authority condition. Do not force-reset or delete another attempt.
actions.evidence: The prepared commit is the target identity that Check compares with the final commit.

actions.title: Inspect the path-handling target
actions.instruction: Read the target and prepared scenario in a native terminal. These are direct terminal commands, never harness passthrough commands, so they never begin with !.
actions.rationale: The model must describe the actual archive-import containment boundary, not a generic security checklist.
actions.expected_result: You can name the learner-controlled input, repository root, and containment-before-write boundary.
actions.recovery: If the target or scenario is missing or locally changed, preserve the attempt and start a new one. Do not substitute another path or alter the target.
actions.evidence: The target must remain byte-identical from Prepare through Check.

actions.title: Have CodeArbiter draft the STRIDE analysis
actions.instruction: In the selected harness, invoke the host-native threat-model command for the exact archive-import target. It is a CodeArbiter command, never a ! terminal passthrough command. The command is read-only: it writes no file and returns advisory STRIDE analysis for your review.
actions.rationale: The opt-in threat-model lane supplies advisory analysis only; a later learner-owned Academy record may summarize it without claiming command output.
actions.expected_result: The command writes no file and returns advisory STRIDE analysis without treating clearance as permission to edit code.
actions.recovery: If the command edits the target, stages, commits, or makes an approval claim, stop. Preserve the attempt and use Reset rather than rewriting history.
actions.evidence: Check does not prove that the agent drafted first or that this command was invoked.

actions.title: Review the draft against the real boundary
actions.instruction: Review the draft yourself. Confirm Scope names controlled archive input, the repository root, and containment or rejection before write. Confirm six distinct STRIDE threats appear in S, T, R, I, D, E order. Treat each control and Clearance as analysis, not authorization.
actions.rationale: A STRIDE heading alone is not a threat model. Each row needs a concrete relationship, category-specific outcome, and control disposition.
actions.expected_result: You can identify a concrete revision or accept a complete, target-specific model.
actions.recovery: If a row is generic, repeated, out of order, or a clearance overclaims authority, ask the agent to revise only the report and review it again before commit.
actions.evidence: Check can reject malformed report evidence. It does not prove that you reviewed the draft.

actions.title: Keep Academy identity evidence separate
actions.instruction: Create learner-owned Academy evidence only after reviewing the read-only advisory output. Verify strict UTF-8 with LF line endings and one final newline. Keep Scope, STRIDE findings, Recommended controls before implementation, and Clearance as the learner-authored summary. Put Academy Target-SHA256/identity binding only after Clearance with exact prepared values.
actions.rationale: The learner-owned Academy evidence explains the review. The separate binding block lets Check bind it to one immutable target without pretending any prose is native ca-threat-model output.
actions.expected_result: The report has four native sections followed by one Academy binding section and no changed path outside the report.
actions.recovery: If Academy labels appear inside a native section or target values are stale, correct the report only. Do not modify academy_engine/paths.py to fit a digest.
actions.evidence: Check validates the target binding and report bytes. It does not prove the host command ran or produced the learner-owned prose.

actions.title: Commit the reviewed report through CodeArbiter
actions.instruction: Only after you accept the report boundary, invoke the host-native commit gate. It is a CodeArbiter harness command, never a ! terminal passthrough command. Commit only .codearbiter/reports/academy/P07-threat-model.md after Prepare.
actions.rationale: One report-only commit keeps final evidence reconstructable and prevents the review becoming a hidden implementation change.
actions.expected_result: One final commit after Prepare adds only the P07 report while academy_engine/paths.py remains unchanged.
actions.recovery: If the commit gate blocks, preserve its finding and correct only the named report boundary in a new attempt. Do not amend, rebase, or add a generic event record.
actions.evidence: The final commit can prove its paths and bytes. It cannot authenticate an approval or conversation.

actions.title: Inspect the report-only commit
actions.instruction: Use a native terminal to inspect the final commit and clean worktree. These are direct terminal commands and never begin with !.
actions.rationale: A local inspection makes path scope and target preservation visible before external Check.

variants.command:
git show --stat --oneline HEAD
git diff HEAD^ HEAD -- academy_engine/paths.py
git status --short

git show --stat --oneline HEAD
git diff HEAD^ HEAD -- academy_engine/paths.py
git status --short

git show --stat --oneline HEAD
git diff HEAD^ HEAD -- academy_engine/paths.py
git status --short

actions.expected_result: The commit adds only the report, the target diff is empty, and git status --short prints nothing.
actions.recovery: If another path changed or the target has a diff, stop and preserve the attempt. Use Reset for a clean retry instead of concealing the extra change.
actions.evidence: This inspection helps you read the final boundary. It does not replace Check.

actions.title: Run the external Academy Check
actions.instruction: Run Check in a native terminal after the report-only commit and clean status. Native-terminal commands never begin with !.
actions.rationale: Academy recomputes target identity, report grammar, Git order, and live worktree outside the learner flow.
actions.expected_result: Check prints checkpoint P07-threat-model: passed and records local progress.
actions.recovery: If Check fails, preserve the committed attempt and read its failed predicate. Use Reset for a new numbered attempt instead of rewriting evidence.
actions.evidence: Check proves report bytes, target identity, allowed history, and clean state. It does not prove that a host command was invoked or that the agent drafted first.

actions.title: Preserve the failed attempt and retry
actions.instruction: Use Reset only when P07 needs another attempt. Run it in a native terminal at the Academy clone root; it archives the earlier attempt before creating the next numbered retry branch. Native-terminal commands never begin with !.
actions.rationale: A retry leaves rejected report evidence reachable instead of destroying it with a force reset or history rewrite.
actions.expected_result: Academy archives the prior attempt and prints the next academy/P07-threat-model/ATTEMPT_NUMBER branch.
actions.recovery: If Reset stops, preserve its message and current branch. Resolve only the named condition; never delete the earlier attempt or alter the frozen target.
actions.evidence: The failed branch remains inspectable while the retry starts from the immutable lesson base.
